does_not_prove.statement: The result is relative to the controller revision, contract draft versions and reason registry named in subject.pinned; it does not carry to any other revision.
No claim that a decision was correct, that a policy was adequate or that a grant was lawfully issued.
Destination ledger rows are executor-written, unsequenced and unsigned: no claim that the ledger is complete or unforged, or that an effect occurred in the world.
A record rewritten with every affected commitment recomputed is accepted (category F); no external anchor exists.
This is a verification report. It is not an attestation, not an Index or BitRep signature and not an authorization; it grants and denies nothing and is never an input to a grant or decision.
An input refused at the wire level is reported as refused; neither the verifier nor this harness normalizes it and runs it again.
Nothing here changes the V1 scope, the failure register, a profile, a pin or any qualified row; this report is report-only and gates nothing.
Agreement between verifier and controller on a corpus is not equivalence outside that corpus.
No figure from any paper is a target, baseline or expectation; the only numbers are counts from the corpora named here, each over its own denominator.
Seed corpora are regression checks (the ODES fixtures were written for rules the validators already implement); detection figures come only from the generated corpus.

A witness that matches the records shows only that match: not that it was published, published in time, held by a party independent of the record keeper, or who published it (the witness record has no signer or proof member). Rows appended after the latest witness digest are not covered, only list-valued run-record ledgers are covered (the destination ledger snapshot is not), and a record and witness rewritten together to agree are accepted (category F). Witnessed populations are measured apart from unwitnessed ones and never pooled.

definitions.noop: the mutant's files are byte-identical to the clean trace's (a structural operator is also noop when its files are canonically equal); the design's wording 'byte-equal after canonicalization' is not used for text operators because a duplicate member or NaN reads as the clean document under Python's parser
definitions.clean_false_rejection: per category, clean traces on which that category's operators produced an effective mutant, rejected by the verifier; benign (B) counts benign mutants
definitions.metric_impact: measures are derived by this harness from the mutant's files (the verifier does not expose them); unavailable for a mutant Python's parser cannot read
definitions.intended_code: the operator's frozen intended codes; a different but correct verifier code counts in any_code only. Catalogue version 2: intended codes frozen post-hoc after run 1 (703cdde1), so intended_code figures are not held-out; any_code detection is the primary figure. Catalogue version 3 (family H): operators written after the verifier's tier V3 existed, intended codes frozen post-hoc from its emitted codes; any_code detection is the primary figure
definitions.known_limit: H4.destination-row-dropped-uncorroborated is a known-limit control (catalogue 3.2): expected accept, labelled post-hoc, because the witness profile does not cover destination.json (ODES decision 30-A, ODES #89). It stays in the H4 row's accept count (the contract has no operator-level expectation) and is listed apart under witnessed.known_limit_controls; it is not a missed detection and is not in per-operator not_rejected.
definitions.expected_abstain: H7 and H8 are controls with expected verdict abstain (the verifier says could_not_check); an accept there is a false acceptance (counted in false_acceptance), a reject a false rejection (it shows as reject in verdicts and detection.any_code, which for these rows is not detection). Exception (catalogue 3.1, ODES decision 30-A): H8.witness-file-absent is an input-error control, expected exit 2 and no report; those runs sit in the row's error count (the contract has no row-level input_error) and are listed apart under witnessed.input_error_controls

x-qualification-harness.intended_codes_status: unwitnessed operators: frozen post-hoc after run 1 (703cdde1), unchanged since catalogue version 2; witnessed operators (family H, catalogue version 3): written after the verifier's tier V3 existed, intended codes frozen post-hoc from the codes it emits; not held-out

witnessed.population: witnessed (family H, with the B and F controls measured on the same witnessed traces); never pooled with the unwitnessed corpora
witnessed.witness_producer: acp witness publish (control plane public command; LocalFileWitness JSON lines)

known_limit_controls.label: known limit, post-hoc
known_limit_controls.reason: the witness profile (witness-digest/0.1) covers the run record's list-valued members, not destination.json, so a destination row that nothing in the record corroborates is as undetectable with a witness as without (R6; ODES decision 30-A, ODES #89)
